name: Garware Hi-Tech Films Ltd
tagline: World's No.1 vertically-integrated chip-to-film specialty-film maker; debt-free with Rs 850cr cash, funded TPU/SCF/PPF expansion, but a 43x P/E after a 123% run and a likely-peak Q1FY27 30% margin
business_overview: Manufactures paint-protection film (PPF), sun-control film (SCF), and other specialty polyester films, largely for automotive and architectural applications, with meaningful export exposure to the US and Middle East.
fundamentals_table: 18% headline; ~25%+ core after adjusting FY17 land-revaluation reserve (independently corroborated)

fundamentals_narrative: Genuinely clean balance sheet - effectively debt-free with ~Rs 850 Cr cash, promoter holding 60.7% unpledged. Core operating ROCE is >25% once capital employed is adjusted for the FY17 land-revaluation reserve (an adjustment independent write-ups corroborate, not just community framing); headline ROCE 18%. FY26 revenue was essentially flat (Rs 2,120 Cr, +0.5%) - a lost year on US tariffs of up to 50% in H1FY26, cut to 10% from Feb-2026. Q1FY27 was the strongest quarter ever: revenue Rs 633 Cr (+28% YoY), EBITDA Rs 192 Cr (+56%), EBITDA margin 30.3% (record, +544 bps), PAT Rs 133 Cr (+60%). That margin is above the through-cycle ~23-25% level and was helped by a US tariff-refund benefit (~Rs 50 Cr net) and richer architectural/specialty mix; management guides FY27 margin back to 25% +/-2% on >Rs 2,500 Cr revenue. Working-capital days roughly doubled to ~146 in the tariff period - the one balance-sheet blemish to watch.
technical_read: Not independently pulled this pass. Stock up ~123% in CY2026 into the deep-dive.
sentiment_summary: Read most recent 50 of 172 posts (Jan 2025 to May 2026), covering a US-tariff-risk debate through to strong Q4FY26 results and funded forward capacity guidance.
community_signal: r8b8 (trusted) posted detailed Q2FY26 concall notes (Nov 2025) despite a soft quarter (revenue -8% YoY, PAT -12% YoY), noting PPF capacity doubling to 600 lakh sq ft and a TPU line commissioning by Oct 2027, with 75% of new capacity earmarked for PPF and 25% for next-gen film solutions. niraj's widely-loved (28 loves) 2025 post argued Trump-era tariffs partly reflect broader de-dollarization dynamics rather than Garware-specific risk. Divyansh_Thakur and prchou83 (Q4FY26, May 2026) independently confirmed record quarterly revenue (Rs 597 Cr, highest-ever) and margin expansion (26.2% EBITDA vs 22% prior year) alongside funded SCF/TPU capacity additions (Rs 191 Cr + Rs 118 Cr capex).
bull_case: Debt-free with ~Rs 850 Cr cash; core operating ROCE >25% (ex FY17 land-revaluation reserve) sustained for years - genuine balance-sheet and franchise quality; describes itself as world's No.1 chip-to-film integrated maker, 87% VAP mix
Q1FY27 delivered real (not just guided) operating leverage - record Rs 633 Cr revenue and a first-ever 30.3% EBITDA margin, +544 bps YoY

Funded, dated capacity pipeline: TPU line commissioning Q3FY27 (guided +1.5-2% margin in FY28, 3 new products in development), new SCF automated lamination line +1,200 LSF/yr (~Rs 550 Cr peak revenue potential, live H1FY28), PPF capacity already doubled
US tariff cut from 50% to 10% (Feb-2026); non-US business grew ~20%; architectural/specialty films now 25%+ of revenue (from ~5%) at the highest margins
bear_case: Valuation has run hard: ~43x trailing P/E after a ~123% CY2026 move - a lot of the TPU/SCF/PPF ramp looks priced in; thesis-fit as a 10x-in-2-3-years name no longer stacks up at ~Rs 16,700 Cr

Q1FY27's 30.3% EBITDA margin is very likely a peak - above the ~23-25% through-cycle band, flattered by a one-off ~Rs 50 Cr tariff-refund benefit and mix; management itself guides FY27 back to 25% +/-2%
FY26 revenue was flat YoY - the multi-year CAGR masks a lost year, and US tariffs remain a live, resettable overhang (currently 10%, was 50%)
Governance history: independent write-ups flag elevated promoter compensation, related-party dealings and a legacy (Garware Polyester) of minority interests not being prioritised
Working-capital days roughly doubled to ~146 during the tariff period - efficiency deterioration to watch
verdict_headline: High-quality, debt-free specialty-film franchise with a funded capacity pipeline - but priced for it at ~43x after a 123% run, with a likely-peak Q1 margin and a flat FY26 in the base
verdict_reasoning: Business quality confirmed by the filings: debt-free, ~Rs 850 Cr cash, core ROCE >25%, dominant integrated position, VAP mix 87%
Growth optionality (TPU Q3FY27, SCF H1FY28, PPF doubling) is funded and dated - not speculative
But the price already reflects it: ~43x trailing, Q1FY27 30.3% margin is above the through-cycle band and helped by a one-off tariff refund, and management guides margin down to 25% +/-2%
At ~Rs 16,700 Cr with 15-20% guided medium-term CAGR, this is a compounder, not a 10x-in-2-3-years or 100x-in-10-years candidate - thesis_fit moved to neither
Conviction eased to Medium: the franchise is intact but risk/reward at this multiple, with peak-margin and governance caveats, is less attractive than when Medium-High was set

deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium-High -> Medium.
